fields.subnational_unit: Karnataka state (Bengaluru, Mysuru, Mandya, Chitradurga, Hubballi-Dharwad, Mangaluru discussed)
fields.population: Karnataka state water governance and water utilities, with Water User Associations
fields.sample_size: not applicable; secondary documents only (Karnataka State Water Policy 2022, National Water Policy 2012, Central Water Commission, Ministry of Jal Shakti, KUWSDB, India Water Partnership 2016, state statistics, peer-reviewed literature); number of documents not stated
fields.effect_measure: qualitative policy-analysis case study with thematic coding on four analytical variables
fields.effect_estimate: Karnataka State Water Policy 2022 adopts IWRM principles and is associated with localised gains: wider micro-irrigation adoption with 'preliminary assessments' of 15-30% higher water productivity, over 8 million litres per day of treated wastewater reused in Bengaluru, and participatory coordination through Water User Associations. Barriers: fragmented mandates among irrigation, urban supply and groundwater agencies, financial constraints, no integrated data platforms, uneven awareness, and inconsistent compliance and enforcement outside Bengaluru. No statistical analysis; the productivity figures are cited preliminary assessments rather than estimates produced by the study.
fields.model_type: qualitative policy analysis of secondary documents
fields.study_design: qualitative policy-analysis case study based exclusively on secondary data
fields.section: Full text (Discover Water, open access): Abstract; Methodology 3.1-3.5; Findings; Discussion and conclusion 6.1-6.2

evidence_level: Policy-analysis case study: a document-based qualitative analysis of Karnataka's 2022 State Water Policy and IWRM implementation, read in full text 2026-10-04. Reports localised gains (micro-irrigation, wastewater reuse, user-association coordination) and institutional fragmentation, weak data systems and uneven enforcement. Secondary documents only; no effect estimate of its own.

notes: DESIGN FLAG: secondary-document policy analysis; Legal Framework rating NOT re-answered. Quantitative claims (15-30% water productivity) are cited preliminary assessments, so no effect-size row.
